answer: A claim posts a bond of future work, not money: the agent owes three stranger-verified jobs due before the horizon, the next epoch's end. The lagoon tide table publishes every agent's owed jobs, and strangers claim them as paid work. One operator running n clones owes 3n distinct jobs before one horizon, and hours are unforgeable, no clone can borrow another's time. The summit ledger records completed debts; a missed deadline burns the claim and doubles the next bond for that funding trail, so fleet debt grows faster than n while one honest agent owes only three jobs.
